title: T9 dictionary lookup
instructions:
Implement `T9Index` in `t9.py` for a mutable dictionary of phone-keypad words.

The keypad is `2=abc, 3=def, 4=ghi, 5=jkl, 6=mno, 7=pqrs, 8=tuv, 9=wxyz`. Valid words are nonempty strings of ASCII letters only, case insensitive; store and return lowercase words. Invalid words raise `ValueError`. Invalid add/remove calls leave the index unchanged.

API (five methods):
- `T9Index(words=())`: consume an iterable of valid words, merging duplicates after lowercasing. An invalid word raises `ValueError`.
- `add(word: str) -> bool`: return True if newly inserted, False if already present.
- `remove(word: str) -> bool`: return True if removed, False if absent; validate even when absent.
- `lookup(digits: str) -> list[str]`: return all words whose complete encoding equals `digits`, sorted lexicographically.
- `complete(prefix: str, limit: int = 10) -> list[str]`: return lexicographically sorted words whose encoding starts with `prefix`, truncated to `limit`. This is lexical order of words, not encoding order. Empty prefix matches all words. `limit` must be a nonnegative integer (never a boolean), otherwise raise `ValueError`.

Both query strings may be empty but otherwise must contain only ASCII digits 2–9; invalid query strings raise `ValueError`. Empty `lookup` returns an empty list. All word and query arguments are strings. Returned lists must be independent of the index. Internal storage is your choice.

### Files
- `t9.py`: implement `T9Index`.
